mo_softball.blurb: Softball is a compact sandstone bouldering sector within Peter's Branch, a remote crag near Sparta in the Missouri Ozarks. The problems sit along a short wall, with a cave facing it, reached by following the trail left of the sunny-side sector. About a dozen problems run from easy V1 and V2 warm-ups up through a cluster of V4 to V6 lines, with a single V10 as the standout hard test. Expect short, powerful moves on slopers and crimps rather than tall lines. Shade and sun conditions here are not well documented, so plan around the weather and bring pads.

mo_goose_island_south_rock.blurb: Of the three sandstone towers at Raven Rocks, on Truman Lake's Pomme de Terre arm, Goose Island is the one farthest south. A tall north-facing wall with a small cave holds most of the lines, and that side stays shaded nearly all day, which helps in summer. Most of the eleven routes are bolted sport, plus one trad line and one top-rope; grades start around 5.5 and cluster between 5.8 and 5.9, with one 5.11 for experienced leads. Water traverses let you drop into the lake. The sandstone is soft for the region, so give it a few days to dry after rain. Top-roping is easy via a scramble to the summit.

mo_funhouse_alcove.blurb: Funhouse Alcove is a limestone alcove in the Warsaw cliffs beside Truman Lake. Seven sport routes and four trad lines go from 5.8 to the low 5.12s, with the bulk at 5.10, so it suits climbers who have outgrown the easy grades. The cliffs are mostly vertical to slightly overhanging, and the wall is reached by the west walkdown, then east at the bottom; at high water, rounding the corner needs some slab traversing. The rock is soft, so a helmet and attentive belaying are wise. The longest route wants a 60 m rope while the rest go with a 50 m, and since you get to the cliff top first, top-roping many lines is an option.

mo_e_apache.blurb: Apache is a sport wall on the south side of Robinson Bluff, a dolomite cliff above the Big River near Tiff. It is a short walk past the foot of the main staircase, beyond the neighbouring wall. Once buried in vines, it has been cleaned up and now offers a mix of steep slab and shaded vertical climbing, with shade through summer afternoons and plenty of sun on winter mornings. The ten routes run from 5.7 to 5.10, with most in the 5.8 to 5.10 range, and there are easy warm-ups at the right end. It makes a good choice for moderate climbers wanting lines that stay comfortable in warm weather.

mo_i_dollywall.blurb: Dollywall is a shaded sport wall on the south side of Robinson Bluff, a dolomite cliff along the Big River in Washington County. It lies between the Dog Walk and City Limits walls, a good way left of the main staircase. Twelve sport routes cover a wide spread, from an easy 5.6 and a few 5.7 to 5.9 lines, up to a heavy block of 5.11s and one 5.12, so it leans toward strong intermediate and advanced leaders. The base of the wall often stays damp, but the rock above the first bolts is clean and dry, so carry a stick-clip for the opening moves.
